text:
lia_sec: Heads up — I found a visibility issue: users with the 'Admin' role can see org-level per-customer usage & cost breakdowns under /console/analytics/usage even when the 'billing_view' permission is supposed to be restricted. :eyes:
eric_eng: can you repro? any recent RBAC refactor that touched billing routes?
lia_sec: repro steps below, done in staging with sandbox org id 3642:
```
GET /api/v1/analytics/usage?org_id=3642
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Response: 200 OK
Body: { "customers": [{"org_id": 111,"tokens": 12_345,"cost_usd": 1_234.56}, ...] }
```
lia_sec: admin-token is role=Admin (not BillingViewer). Should have returned 403.
maria_sre: that endpoint should call `authz.check('billing:read', org_id)` — maybe the mapping from roles->permissions missed Admin in a mapping change last week.
devon_prodsec: we did a roles/permission refactor in #3118 — I added an alias mapping for `Admin` -> `ALL` in the authz cache to simplify checks. Could be the cause.
eric_eng: logs from staging? lia, can you paste the request log + authz decision?
lia_sec: pasted logs (redacted):
```
[2026-02-11T14:22:11Z] req_id=abc123 method=GET path=/api/v1/analytics/usage user=lia-admin role=Admin org=3642
[2026-02-11T14:22:11Z] authz.decide req_id=abc123 principal=lia-admin check="billing:read" result=ALLOW (source=role-alias-cache)
```
ashley_ds: looks like the decision source is role-alias-cache — that aligns with devon's change.
devon_prodsec: ack, I can reproduce locally. The alias mapping inadvertently treated Admin as if it had billing:read. The intent was Admin -> org:manage not BillingViewer. I'll open a quick revert.
eric_eng: before revert, we need mitigation — this touches production data visibility for cost. Any quick ACL we can apply?
maria_sre: we can toggle the analytics service feature-flag `analytics_v1_open` to false to block the endpoint globally for non-internal roles while we patch. That will impact some dashboards; ping product.
devon_prodsec: creating PR to revert the alias change now, PR #3257.
lia_sec: audit-bot — can you confirm whether any real customer PII or invoices were exposed? We care about billing numbers only (cost/usage).
audit-bot: Audit log created: event_id=evt-789, type=authz_misconfig_exposure, affected_orgs=[111,222,333], users_with_access=[lia-admin,eric-admin], timeframe=2026-02-11T13:45Z..2026-02-11T14:30Z
eric_eng: good catch. Need timeline + who/what accessed. Lia can you pull cloudfront/access logs for that window?
lia_sec: on it, I have the s3 query running. Early results: three accesses from internal admin users and one from a support engineer. No external API keys observed.
ashley_ds: Does this mean cost data landed in support tickets? We should search Intercom for anything referencing unusual billing numbers.
maria_sre: I'll block the analytics route behind a stricter check for `internal_service=true` until the rollback is deployed — low blast radius change.
devon_prodsec: rolled out PR #3257 to staging, running unit + contract tests. Failure mode: we must ensure role aliases are not used for `billing:read` decisions. Test included.
eric_eng: timeline?
devon_prodsec: staging deploy in 10m, prod can go in 30m if green.
lia_sec: please add KMS audit: were any billing exports encrypted with the customer KMS key and accessed? We need to know if any keys were used cross-org.
audit-bot: KMS access log check queued (query id q-412).
ashley_ds: also add a regression test to the analytics e2e suite that asserts `Admin` cannot see per-customer cost unless `BillingViewer` granted.
devon_prodsec: added test in PR, pushed.
deploy-bot: staging deploy for commit 9f3a7 scheduled (analytics service) — CI green.
maria_sre: staging looks good, no more allow decisions for Admin. Rolling to prod now with a kill-switch ready.
eric_eng: after prod deploy, run a backfill audit: list all allow decisions for billing:read in the affected timeframe and export to secure s3 path. Lia, can you coordinate?
lia_sec: will do. Also recommend we rotate any short-lived tokens used by support during that window and notify compliance.
devon_prodsec: prod deploy complete. PR #3257 merged.
lia_sec: prod logs show no further unauthorized allows after 2026-02-11T15:05Z.
audit-bot: Backfill complete. event_id=evt-790, allow_decisions_found=14, affected_usernames=[u1,u2,u3], export_path=s3://redwood-security/audit/2026-02-11/authz-billing-read.csv.gpg
ashley_ds: next steps for postmortem: 1) root cause — role-alias mapping regression from #3118; 2) short-term — revert + feature flag + audit export; 3) medium — add e2e ingress-level check for billing endpoints; 4) long-term — formal approval gating for role->permission changes + canary in authz cache. I'll draft the postmortem.
eric_eng: assign owners and SLA for notifications. Lia -> contact compliance + customer support for disclosure decision. Maria -> ops mitigation. Devon -> fix + test + PR process update. Ashley -> postmortem + eval impact on analytics dashboards.
lia_sec: will notify compliance and start a disclosure checklist. Draft message ready, holding until legal OK. :white_check_mark:
eric_eng: thanks everyone. Good catch and fast turnaround.
lia_sec: FYI I added a quick defensive audit rule to alert on any non-BillingViewer roles accessing billing endpoints (alert severity=high).
